title: Beyond Instrumental and Substitutive Paradigms: Introducing Machine Culture as an Emergent Phenomenon in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating models of US and Chinese origins using an 8-task multimodal battery that measures cross-cultural psychological differences in cognitive styles (e.g., holistic vs. analytic processing, causal attribution, categorization) and affective styles (e.g., high vs. low arousal ideal affect) to test alignment with established East Asian or Western human benchmarks.

Comparing model outputs across identical tasks prompted in English versus Chinese to evaluate if language activates specific cultural mindsets (the 'Substitutive Paradigm') or instead triggers structural asymmetries like verbosity and affective intensity biases linked to the training data of specific languages.
